mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes SL 500 or SL 560 engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt M113 engine for the SL 500 costs £3,200-£4,800 supply-only; a rebuilt M273 costs £4,000-£5,800; a rebuilt M278 costs £4,500-£6,500; a rebuilt M176 for the SL 560 costs £6,500-£12,000 supply-only. Fitting adds £1,200-£2,500 depending on complexity - V8 work requires specialist knowledge.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of PCV oil separator failure on a Mercedes SL 560 (M176)?

acceptedAnswer.text: A high-pitched whistling noise at idle, rough idle, or a check engine light are the classic warning signs on the M176 engine. If ignored, it leads to a blown rear main seal and a massive oil leak. Mercedes-Benz mandates that both oil separators be replaced whenever a rear main seal is found leaking.

mainEntity.name: Is the Mercedes SL 500 or SL 560 V8 engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: Each generation has its own character and weaknesses. The M113 is generally robust but oil pump chain stretch is common. The M273 suffers from balance shaft/idler gear wear on early units. The M278 has timing chain tensioner and cylinder scoring issues. The M176 is powerful but the PCV oil separator is a notorious failure point. With these addressed, all are capable of 100,000+ miles.

mainEntity.name: How long do Mercedes SL 500 and SL 560 V8 engines last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Properly maintained M113 engines routinely reach 150,000-200,000 miles. The M273, M278 and M176 are too new for definitive long-term data, but with proactive maintenance on known issues, 100,000-150,000 miles is achievable.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in my Mercedes SL 500 or SL 560?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the SL is otherwise in good condition with no rust or major transmission faults. A rebuilt M113 costs £3,200-£4,800 - far less than replacing a £6,000-£18,000 vehicle. The SL 560's higher value (£30,000-£55,000) makes replacement even more financially justifiable.

mainEntity.name: What oil does my Mercedes SL 500 or SL 560 V8 need?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mercedes-Benz specifies MB 229.5 high-performance oil - typically 5W-30 or 5W-40 fully synthetic. The M113 requires approximately 8.0 litres; the M273 requires approximately 8.5 litres; the M278 requires approximately 9.0 litres; the M176 requires approximately 9.5 litres.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes Benz SL 500/560 - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The SL 500 has been the heart of the SL range across four generations, powered by a succession of V8 engines that have defined Mercedes grand touring excellence. The SL 560 badge, originally used on the R107 (1985-1989) with the M117 5.6-litre V8, was revived in the modern era for the R231 facelift with the M176 4.0-litre twin-turbo V8. The SL 500 lineage spans the M113 5.0-litre V8 in the R230 (2001-2006), the M273 5.5-litre V8 in the R230 facelift (2006-2011), and the M278 4.7-litre twin-turbo V8 in the early R231 (2012-2017). These V8s represent the pinnacle of SL performance and refinement, each with its own character and engineering story.

However, each has well-documented weaknesses that can lead to significant repair costs. The M117 suffers from timing chain guide degradation, the M113 from oil pump chain stretch, the M273 from balance shaft wear, the M278 from timing chain and cylinder issues, and the M176 from PCV oil separator failure leading to rear main seal leaks. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.group: M176 PCV Oil Separator & Rear Main Seal Failure
problems.h4: M176 PCV Oil Separator & Rear Main Seal Failure - The Modern SL 560's Critical Weakness
problems.rootCause: One of the most notorious design flaws on the M176/M177 engines is the failure of the Positive Crankcase Ventilation (PCV) oil separators. Heat bakes the internal diaphragms. A failing separator will often cause a high-pitched whistling noise at idle, a rough idle, or a check engine light. Eventually, increased crankcase pressure finds the weakest point - the rear main crankshaft oil seal (RMS) - causing a massive oil leak. Mercedes-Benz mandates that both oil separators be replaced whenever a rear main seal is found leaking to prevent a repeat failure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Diagnostic scan, crankcase pressure test, inspect oil separators
repairOptions.longevity: Confirms whether separator or seal is the root cause

repairOptions.longevity: If caught before seal damage occurs

repairOptions.longevity: If oil loss has caused bearing or bottom-end damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2018-2020 SL 560 is worth approximately £30,000-£55,000 depending on mileage and condition. The SL 560 sits firmly in the £15,000+ band - replacement cost is typically small relative to vehicle value, making a full rebuilt engine a justifiable investment for owners of these high-value flagships.
problems.recommendation: The oil separator is the root cause of most M176 rear main seal leaks. If you hear a whistling noise at idle, notice a rough idle, or see a check engine light, have the PCV system checked immediately. If caught early, replacing the oil separators alone (£1,200-£1,800 at a specialist) prevents the much more expensive rear main seal replacement. If the rear main seal has already failed, replacing both the seal and the oil separators together is the only sensible approach. On an SL 560 worth £30,000-£55,000, the full rebuilt engine route is justifiable if bottom-end damage has occurred.
